title: Jack Dorsey’s Free AI Agent Changes Everything
description:
The #1 community for building a highly-profitable personal brand with AI and Claude Code.
👉 https://www.skool.com/buildroom/

Summary ⤵️

While everyone is debating Claude vs ChatGPT, a powerful open-source AI agent is flying under the radar.

It’s called Goose.

Built by the team at Block, Goose is designed to work with multiple AI models instead of locking you into a single provider.

Here’s why people are paying attention:

→ Works with Claude, GPT, Gemini, DeepSeek, and more
→ Open source
→ Reads files and executes workflows
→ Helps automate coding tasks
→ No vendor lock-in

Setup is simple:

Install Goose
Connect your preferred model/API
Give it tasks in plain English

Reality check:

No AI agent is truly “set and forget.”
You still need to review outputs, especially for production code and business-critical tasks.

But if you want flexibility without being tied to one ecosystem, Goose is worth looking at.

transcript: The guy who built Twitter just gave away a million-dollar AI agent for free and almost nobody noticed because everyone's too busy watching the Claude versus ChatGPT fight. I'm not even exaggerating. Let me show you what this thing does. So, it's called Goose, built by Jack Dorsey over at Block. He literally used it to replace 4,000 employees and it now writes 90% of Block's code. Pretty freaking cool. Now, here's the part that's really cool. Every other agent, Claude, Coda, Cursor, all of them locks you to one company. Goose works with any model, Claude, GPT, Gemini, Deep Seek, whatever. You switch [music] in one line, zero lock-in. And the setup is stupidly simple, three steps. First, one terminal command and Goose is installed. Second, plug in any AI model API key. Third, type your task in plain English. That's it. From there, Goose reads your files, writes the code, runs the tests, and ships the product. Free, open source, no login. Super, super cool. If you want the full setup guide for Goose, check my pinned comment below for the link.
